agent_primer:
AutoCAD is Autodesk's industry-standard 2D/3D drafting CAD application. It is both keyboard-driven (via a typed command line) and ribbon-driven (via tabbed toolbars at the top). Most experienced AutoCAD users live in the command line — typing `LINE` or `L` then `Enter` is faster than clicking the Line tool in the ribbon. The seed shortcuts here lean heavily on typed commands because they are the most version-stable and locale-stable surface in AutoCAD.

**The command line is the canonical interaction surface.** It sits docked at the bottom of the application window and shows the active prompt sequence (e.g. `Specify first point:` after typing `LINE`). Most AutoCAD operations take the form: type the command name (or its alias), press Enter, follow the prompts. AutoCAD aliases are short — `L` for LINE, `C` for CIRCLE, `M` for MOVE, `O` for OFFSET, `TR` for TRIM. Aliases live in `acad.pgp`; users can add their own. v0 seeds use the published Autodesk defaults.

**On macOS the command line panel can be toggled with `cmd+9`.** When the panel is hidden, typing on the canvas still works — any letter triggers the command-line autocomplete dropdown — but for scripted control we explicitly toggle the panel visible and type into it. Several seed shortcuts use the action chain: `cmd+9` (ensure panel visible), `type_text` (the command alias), `enter` (submit). On a system where the command line is already visible, the first `cmd+9` toggle will hide it; the second one re-shows it. This is acceptable for v0 — the chain still ends with the command line visible and the command sent.

**Key concepts an agent must understand:**
- **Model space vs paper space.** Model space is where you draw at real-world scale; paper space (layouts) is where you compose printed sheets. Many drawings have multiple layouts (tabs at the bottom of the canvas).
- **Layers** are the primary organizing primitive. Every object has a layer. Layers can be turned off, frozen, locked, or have their color/lineweight set. The `LAYER` command (alias `LA`) opens the Layer Properties Manager.
- **Blocks** are reusable named groups of geometry, like symbols. `INSERT` (alias `I`) places one; `BLOCK` (alias `B`) creates one from selected geometry. **Xrefs** (external references) are similar but reference an external `.dwg` file; useful for collaborative drafting.
- **Object Snaps (OSNAP)** make the cursor snap to geometric features — endpoint, midpoint, center, intersection, perpendicular, tangent, nearest. Toggle with `F3` (or status bar). Persistent OSNAP modes are set in the `OSNAP` dialog (alias `OS`).
- **UCS (User Coordinate System)** lets you redefine the X/Y/Z axes for drafting in arbitrary planes. Important in 3D.
- **Polar tracking, Ortho mode, Dynamic input** — drafting aids on the status bar (toggled with F8, F10, F12 respectively).

**Ribbon tabs (top):** Home, Insert, Annotate, Parametric, View, Manage, Output, Add-ins, Collaborate, Express Tools. Many seed shortcuts route through typed commands rather than ribbon clicks because the ribbon is laid out differently across versions.

**Status bar (bottom):** toggles for Grid (F7), Snap (F9), Ortho (F8), Polar (F10), OSNAP (F3), Object Snap Tracking (F11), Dynamic UCS (F6), Dynamic Input (F12), Lineweight, Annotation Scale.

**Important command-line behavior:** typing a command while another command is in progress usually does not cancel it cleanly. The pre_step in this app's workflow presses Escape before each shortcut to clear any in-progress command, dismiss any dynamic-input prompt, or close the autocomplete dropdown. This is critical for reliable scripted control.

**Save behavior:** `cmd+S` saves to the current `.dwg` file. New drawings prompt for a path. `SAVEAS` (or `cmd+shift+S`) opens the Save Drawing As dialog where the format dropdown selects between `.dwg`, `.dwt` (template), `.dxf` (exchange format), and older drawing versions for backward compatibility. Default save format is `.dwg`.

**Verification on AutoCAD is hard.** The drawing canvas is opaque to the macOS accessibility tree (custom OpenGL view). The command-line history shows what the agent typed and AutoCAD's response, but is not exposed cleanly in v0. Most seed shortcuts verify with `interpret_check` (vision) — the agent looks at the screen and judges whether the expected geometric / dialog state is present. File-system writes (save, plot to PDF) verify well via `file_check` in principle, though seed shortcuts default to `interpret_check` for consistency.

**Version notes:** this seed targets AutoCAD for Mac 2024+. Earlier versions may differ on the default location of some Express Tools commands and on the Render workspace layout. macOS-only for v0; the underlying MCP `os.action` paths are macOS-only.
